chunks: From him, from Safwan, from al-Walid ibn Hisham, who said:

I arrived from Egypt with some slaves. The tax collector asked me, and I said, 'They are all free.' Then I arrived in Medina and entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and informed him of what I had said to the tax collector. He said, 'There is no blame on you.' I said, 'Among them was a female slave with whom I had intercourse, and she was pregnant.' He said, 'Her child is not the one who frees her; when her master dies, she becomes part of her child's share (of inheritance).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pregnant slave woman's status and inheritance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of *Umm al-Walad* (mother of the child) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the Sunni view where the child's birth often triggers immediate emancipation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the mother remains a slave until the master's death, at which point she becomes free and her freedom is considered part of the estate distributed among the heirs. This ruling highlights the specific Shia interpretation of inheritance mechanics regarding concubines and their offspring.
